brief: An island-town cottage lot: Lester Hubbard House, a 19th-century Lake Erie house; see the photo for its massing, porch and trim. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: the Lake Erie shore towns that stand in for Victory Bay's island streets (Vermilion, Sandusky, Put-in-Bay) were built 1840-1920, and Commons has almost no newer cottages there. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Lester Hubbard House (Sandusky, 1850s): a two-storey limestone Italianate with paired brackets, tall stone chimneys, a side wing with an arcaded porch, a columned entry porch; an iron fence and a sign -- now a museum/guest house

why.note: Sandusky sits on Columbus limestone, quarried in town: its 19th-century houses are grey limestone
